scene.label: Act 1, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. On a ship at sea; a tempestuous noise of thunder and lightning heard.
scene.location: On a ship at sea; a tempestuous noise of thunder and lightning heard.

content.text: Enter a Shipmaster and a Boatswain severally.

lines.text: Boatswain!
lines.plainText: Boatswain

lines.text: Here, master: what cheer?
lines.plainText: Here master what cheer

lines.text: Good! Speak to the mariners: fall to 't yarely, or we run ourselves aground: bestir, bestir.
lines.plainText: Good Speak to the mariners fall to 't yarely or we run ourselves aground bestir bestir

lines.text: Heigh, my hearts! cheerly, cheerly, my hearts! yare, yare! Take in the topsail. Tend to th' master's whistle. Blow till thou burst thy wind, if room enough.
lines.plainText: Heigh my hearts cheerly cheerly my hearts yare yare Take in the topsail Tend to th' master's whistle Blow till thou burst thy wind if room enough

content.text: Enter Alonso, Sebastian, Antonio, Ferdinand, Gonzalo and others.

lines.text: Good boatswain, have care. Where's the master?
lines.plainText: Good boatswain have care Where's the master

lines.text: Play the men.
lines.plainText: Play the men

lines.text: I pray now, keep below.
lines.plainText: I pray now keep below

lines.text: Where is the master, boson?
lines.plainText: Where is the master boson

lines.text: Do you not hear him? You mar our labour: keep your cabins: you do assist the storm.
lines.plainText: Do you not hear him You mar our labour keep your cabins you do assist the storm

lines.text: Nay, good, be patient.
lines.plainText: Nay good be patient

lines.text: When the sea is. Hence! What cares these roarers for the name of king? To cabin! silence! Trouble us not.
lines.plainText: When the sea is Hence What cares these roarers for the name of king To cabin silence Trouble us not

lines.text: Good, yet remember whom thou hast aboard.
lines.plainText: Good yet remember whom thou hast aboard

lines.text: None that I more love than myself. You are a counsellor: if you can command these elements to silence, and work the peace of the present, we will not hand a rope more. Use your authority: if you cannot, give thanks you have lived so long, and make yourself ready in your cabin for the mischance of the hour, if it so hap.—Cheerly, good hearts!—Out of our way, I say.
lines.plainText: None that I more love than myself You are a counsellor if you can command these elements to silence and work the peace of the present we will not hand a rope more Use your authority if you cannot give thanks you have lived so long and make yourself ready in your cabin for the mischance of the hour if it so hapCheerly good heartsOut of our way I say

lines.text: I have great comfort from this fellow. Methinks he hath no drowning mark upon him. His complexion is perfect gallows. Stand fast, good Fate, to his hanging! Make the rope of his destiny our cable, for our own doth little advantage! If he be not born to be hang'd, our case is miserable.
lines.plainText: I have great comfort from this fellow Methinks he hath no drowning mark upon him His complexion is perfect gallows Stand fast good Fate to his hanging Make the rope of his destiny our cable for our own doth little advantage If he be not born to be hang'd our case is miserable

lines.text: Down with the topmast! yare! lower, lower! Bring her to try wi' th' maincourse.
lines.plainText: Down with the topmast yare lower lower Bring her to try wi' th' maincourse

lines.text: A pox o' your throat, you bawling, blasphemous, incharitable dog!
lines.plainText: A pox o' your throat you bawling blasphemous incharitable dog

lines.text: Work you, then.
lines.plainText: Work you then

lines.text: Hang, cur, hang, you whoreson, insolent noisemaker! We are less afraid to be drowned than thou art.
lines.plainText: Hang cur hang you whoreson insolent noisemaker We are less afraid to be drowned than thou art

lines.text: I'll warrant him for drowning, though the ship were no stronger than a nutshell, and as leaky as an unstanched wench.
lines.plainText: I'll warrant him for drowning though the ship were no stronger than a nutshell and as leaky as an unstanched wench

lines.text: Lay her a-hold, a-hold! Set her two courses: off to sea again: lay her off.
lines.plainText: Lay her ahold ahold Set her two courses off to sea again lay her off

lines.text: All lost! to prayers, to prayers! all lost!
lines.plainText: All lost to prayers to prayers all lost

lines.text: What, must our mouths be cold?
lines.plainText: What must our mouths be cold

lines.text: The King and Prince at prayers! Let's assist them,
lines.plainText: The King and Prince at prayers Let's assist them

lines.text: For our case is as theirs.
lines.plainText: For our case is as theirs

lines.text: I am out of patience.
lines.plainText: I am out of patience

lines.text: We are merely cheated of our lives by drunkards.
lines.plainText: We are merely cheated of our lives by drunkards

lines.text: This wide-chapp'd rascal—would thou might'st lie drowning
lines.plainText: This widechapp'd rascalwould thou might'st lie drowning

lines.text: The washing of ten tides!
lines.plainText: The washing of ten tides

lines.text: He'll be hang'd yet,
lines.plainText: He'll be hang'd yet

lines.text: Though every drop of water swear against it,
lines.plainText: Though every drop of water swear against it

lines.text: And gape at wid'st to glut him.
lines.plainText: And gape at wid'st to glut him

lines.text: Let's all sink wi' th' King.
lines.plainText: Let's all sink wi' th' King

lines.text: Let's take leave of him.
lines.plainText: Let's take leave of him

lines.text: Now would I give a thousand furlongs of sea for an acre of barren ground. Long heath, brown furze, anything. The wills above be done! but I would fain die a dry death.
lines.plainText: Now would I give a thousand furlongs of sea for an acre of barren ground Long heath brown furze anything The wills above be done but I would fain die a dry death
